title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LE_0RA0LC_0RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LE_0RA0LC_0RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps and proves the sweeps and the turn at the right end for every length (lean/Sweep.lean). The plain C simulator finds no halt in the first 1011 steps. The counter at the left, which decides where each sweep turns back, is described only from observation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps and the turn at the right end
claims.text: With P = 11111010, Q = 01010010 and W = 11110101 (so P^n 1 = 1 W^n): state A turns A> Q^n into P^n A> in 8n steps; state C turns W^n 1010 C> 101 into 1010 C> 101 Q^n in 30n steps (a shift rule with a word carried on each side, so the file proves cross_l2). Composed with the turn at the right end: A> Q^(n+4) 0101 comes back as 1 1010 C> 101 Q^(n+4) in 38n + 169 steps, and A> Q^(n+4) as 1 1010 C> 101 Q^(n+3) 0101 in 38n + 139 steps, for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The plain simulator of tools/c/tm.h (c/snap.c) runs 1011 steps from blank tape without a halt.

claims.title: A counter of groups at the left
claims.text: Left of the long run of P the tape is a row of groups 11 P^a s P^b s' P^c, the separators s, s' being one of 111010, 101111, 101011, 111111. Each leftward sweep passes through the last few groups and changes their separators and lengths by one; the group lengths grow roughly geometrically from left to right. Right of the long run lie runs of Q (for example Q^269 010101 Q^542 at 3·107 steps); the nearest one loses 8 words every two round trips while the last group gains 8, and when it is used up a new group is built.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when state F reads a 1. The sweeps and turns proved in Lean never do; a halt could only come from the work at the left turn, on the counter, whose exact rule has not been found.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine sweeps back and forth over most of its tape, turning one 8-cell word into another and back. Where each sweep turns around is decided by a counter at the left end, made of groups of runs separated by small digits. The sweeping is proved in Lean; the counter has only been watched.

facts.text: No halt, on the plain simulator.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.522).
After 109 steps the tape spans 52,296 cells (37 left of the start, 38,610 right), with a density of 1s of 0.721.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Two 8-cell words and a counter
html: Most of the tape is a run of P = 11111010 or of Q = 01010010. The head sweeps right turning every Q into a P (8 steps a word), turns at the right end, and sweeps left turning P back into Q (30 steps a word, zig-zagging with the word 1010 on its left and 101 on its right). Each round trip makes the tape a few cells wider, which is why it grows like the square root of the step count.

Where the leftward sweep stops is decided at the left end, where the tape is a row of groups 11 P^a s P^b s' P^c with separators s, s' from 111010, 101111, 101011, 111111. Here is the tape at five consecutive turns at the right end, with the runs of P and Q counted:

sections.heading: The bouncer part is exact
html: Lean proves both sweeps for every number of words and their composition with the turn at the right end: A> Q^(n+4) 0101 comes back as 1 1010 C> 101 Q^(n+4) in exactly 38n + 169 steps, and A> Q^(n+4) as 1 1010 C> 101 Q^(n+3) 0101 in 38n + 139 steps (round_a, round_b). The leftward sweep needs a shift rule with a word carried on both sides of the head, cross_l2, which the file proves by induction.

sections.heading: A counter of groups
html: In the sample above the last group cycles 101011 / 101011 → 111111 / 111111 → 101011 / 101011 with its first two runs one longer every second trip and its last run 5, then 1, longer; the group before it cycles its second separator through 101011, 111111, 111010, 101111, one step per trip, and its runs shift by one between neighbours. So each leftward sweep runs through the last few groups, changing each a little, and turns at a group that is not ready to pass the change on, like the carry of a counter.

Further right the tape keeps runs of Q (Q^269 010101 Q^542 at 3·107 steps): the nearest one loses 8 words every two round trips and the last group gains 8 (1 + 1 + 6), until it is used up and a new group 11 P^2 101011 P^2 101011 P^14 appears. The group lengths grow roughly geometrically from left to right.

sections.heading: Only at the counter
html: The machine halts when state F reads a 1. The proved sweeps and turns never do, so a halt can only come from the work at the left turn, on the counter. An exact rule for that work, as a function of the group lengths and separators, would turn the run into an explicit recursion; it has not been found.

sections.heading: Proved, computed, observed
html: Lean, kernel: the halting configurations; no halt in 10,000 steps; the sweeps, the turns at the right end and the two round-trip halves for every n (lean/Sweep.lean). Lean, native_decide: no halt in 107 steps.
Computed (trusted): no halt in 1011 steps on the plain simulator. Observed: the counter of groups and the runs of Q that it eats.

family: bouncer over a counter of grouped runs
summary: A bouncer: the head sweeps between a counter at the left and the right end, turning an 8-cell word P into Q and back. The counter is a row of groups 11 P^a s P^b s' P^c whose separators cycle through four 6-cell digits; how far left each sweep reaches is set by the counter, and a run of Q at the right is eaten a few words per trip until a new group is built.
